question: Can Codex CLI use a llama.cpp server, and what config does it need?
report:
# Codex CLI Integration with llama.cpp: Configuration Guide and Technical Analysis

## Overview

Codex CLI, OpenAI's command-line coding agent, can indeed be configured to use a llama.cpp server as its inference backend. This integration is achieved through llama.cpp's OpenAI-compatible HTTP API, which exposes endpoints that Codex CLI natively understands. The configuration is straightforward, requiring modifications to a TOML configuration file at `~/.codex/config.toml`. This capability has become increasingly practical as local models have reached quality levels sufficient for production coding tasks, with models like Gemma 4 26B achieving 77.1% on LiveCodeBench v6 and Qwen3.5 27B reaching 80.7% ([Luuong, 2026](https://luongnv89.substack.com/p/how-to-run-claude-code-codex-with)).

## How the Integration Works

The technical mechanism behind this integration relies on llama.cpp's `llama-server` component, which implements an OpenAI-compatible REST API. Codex CLI communicates with the server using the `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint, which follows the OpenAI chat completions format ([pchalasani, 2026](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/blob/main/docs/local-llm-setup.md)). This is distinct from Claude Code, which uses the Anthropic-compatible `/v1/messages` endpoint. Both endpoints are served simultaneously by `llama-server`, meaning a single server instance can serve both Claude Code and Codex CLI at the same time ([pchalasani, 2026](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/blob/main/docs/local-llm-setup.md)).

The architecture follows a simple pattern: start `llama-server` with a model loaded (making it available at a local endpoint such as port 8123), then configure Codex CLI to point to that endpoint ([pchalasani, 2026](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/blob/main/docs/local-llm-setup.md)). The `wire_api` field in the configuration determines which protocol Codex CLI uses to communicate with the server.

## Basic Configuration

The primary configuration file for Codex CLI is located at `~/.codex/config.toml`. To connect Codex CLI to a llama.cpp server, you need to define a model provider entry. The minimal configuration looks as follows:

```toml
model = "glm-4.7-flash"
model_reasoning_effort = "medium"
model_provider = "llamacpp"

[model_providers.llamacpp]
name = "llamacpp"
base_url = "http://localhost:8080/v1"
```

([Tammam, 2026](https://tammam.io/blog/llama-cpp-setup-with-claude-codex-cli))

An alternative configuration format uses the `wire_api` field to explicitly specify the protocol:

```toml
[model_providers.llama-local]
name = "Local LLM via llama.cpp"
base_url = "http://localhost:8123/v1"
wire_api = "chat"
```

([pchalasani, 2026](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/blob/main/docs/local-llm-setup.md))

The `wire_api` field accepts values such as `"chat"` (for the `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint) or `"responses"` (for the `/v1/responses` endpoint). The choice depends on which endpoint your llama.cpp server exposes and which protocol your model supports. For most standard llama.cpp deployments, `"chat"` is the appropriate value ([pchalasani, 2026](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/blob/main/docs/local-llm-setup.md)).

## Starting the llama.cpp Server

Before configuring Codex CLI, you must start a `llama-server` instance. A typical command for serving a model looks like:

```bash
llama-server -hf unsloth/GLM-4.7-Flash-GGUF:UD-Q4_K_XL \
  --alias glm-4.7-flash \
  --jinja \
  --temp 0.7 --top-p 1.0 --min-p 0.01 --fit on \
  --sleep-idle-seconds 300 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080
```

([Tammam, 2026](https://tammam.io/blog/llama-cpp-setup-with-claude-codex-cli))

Key parameters include `--jinja` for proper chat template rendering, `--fit on` for automatic memory optimization, and `--sleep-idle-seconds` for GPU memory management. The `--host 0.0.0.0` flag is necessary when running inside Docker or when remote access is needed; otherwise, the server defaults to `127.0.0.1` ([Glukhov, 2026](https://www.glukhov.org/llm-hosting/llama-cpp/)).

For Docker-based deployments:

```bash
docker run --gpus all -p 8080:8080 \
  ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda \
  -hf unsloth/GLM-4.7-Flash-GGUF:UD-Q4_K_XL \
  --jinja --temp 0.7 --top-p 1.0 --min-p 0.01 --fit on \
  --sleep-idle-seconds 300 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080
```

([Tammam, 2026](https://tammam.io/blog/llama-cpp-setup-with-claude-codex-cli))

## Multi-Model Configuration

For users who need to switch between multiple models without editing the TOML file, Codex CLI supports command-line overrides using the `--model` and `-c` (config) flags:

```bash
# Use GPT-OSS-20B on port 8123
codex --model gpt-oss-20b -c model_provider=llama-8123

# Use Qwen3-30B on port 8124
codex --model qwen3-30b -c model_provider=llama-8124
```

([pchalasani, 2026](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/blob/main/docs/local-llm-setup.md))

This requires defining multiple providers in the configuration file:

```toml
[model_providers.llama-8123]
name = "Local LLM port 8123"
base_url = "http://localhost:8123/v1"
wire_api = "chat"

[model_providers.llama-8124]
name = "Local LLM port 8124"
base_url = "http://localhost:8124/v1"
wire_api = "chat"
```

([pchalasani, 2026](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/blob/main/docs/local-llm-setup.md))

## Router Mode with Config File

For advanced setups where multiple models are managed by a single llama.cpp server process, the router mode with `--models-preset` is the recommended approach. This requires creating a configuration file at `~/llama-cpp/config.ini`:

```ini
[*]
# Global settings
jinja = true

[glm-4.7-flash]
hf-repo = unsloth/GLM-4.7-Flash-GGUF:UD-Q4_K_XL
jinja = true
temp = 0.7
ctx-size = 32768
top-p = 1
min-p = 0.01
fa = auto
```

The server is then launched with:

```bash
llama-server \
  --models-preset ~/llama-cpp/config.ini \
  --sleep-idle-seconds 300 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 --models-max 1
```

([Tammam, 2026](https://tammam.io/blog/llama-cpp-setup-with-claude-codex-cli))

The `--models-max 1` flag ensures only one model is loaded in GPU memory at a time, with models loaded on demand based on what clients request. The `--sleep-idle-seconds 300` flag unloads models after 5 minutes of inactivity, freeing GPU memory ([Tammam, 2026](https://tammam.io/blog/llama-cpp-setup-with-claude-codex-cli)).

## Vision Model Support

Codex CLI supports image inputs via the `-i` or `--image` flags, and llama.cpp can serve vision-language models for local multimodal inference. However, vision only works via the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint (Codex CLI), not the Anthropic `/v1/messages` endpoint (Claude Code) ([pchalasani, 2026](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/blob/main/docs/local-llm-setup.md)).

Vision models require two GGUF files: the main model and a multimodal projector (mmproj). For example, with Gemma-4-26B:

```bash
llama-server -hf unsloth/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-GGUF:UD-Q4_K_XL \
  --mmproj ~/models/mmproj-BF16.gguf \
  --port 8132 \
  -c 131072 -b 2048 -ub 1024 \
  --parallel 1 -fa on --jinja \
  --temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 64
```

The corresponding Codex CLI configuration:

```toml
[model_providers.llama-8132]
name = "Gemma-4 Vision"
base_url = "http://localhost:8132/v1"
wire_api = "chat"
```

Usage: `codex --model gemma-4 -c model_provider=llama-8132 -i screenshot.png "describe this"` ([pchalasani, 2026](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/blob/main/docs/local-llm-setup.md)).

## Performance and Memory Tuning

Several llama.cpp flags are relevant for optimizing Codex CLI performance:

| Flag | Purpose | Recommendation |
|------|---------|----------------|
| `--fit` | Automatic memory optimization | Enable with `on` |
| `--sleep-idle-seconds` | Unload model after idle period | Tune to usage pattern (e.g., 300) |
| `-fa` / `--flash-attn` | Flash Attention for KV cache reduction | Enable (`on` or `auto`) |
| `-ngl N` | Offload N layers to GPU | Set to maximum for your VRAM |
| `-c` | Context window size | Minimum 64K for agentic use |
| `--parallel` | Concurrent request limit | Lower for memory savings |

([Tammam, 2026](https://tammam.io/blog/llama-cpp-setup-with-claude-codex-cli); [4SAPI, 2026](https://blog.4sapi.com/blog/llama-cpp-local-deployment-guide))

A critical consideration is that both Claude Code and Codex CLI require a model with at least a 64K context window for reliable agentic use ([Luuong, 2026](https://luongnv89.substack.com/p/how-to-run-claude-code-codex-with)). When a model is unloaded after the idle timeout, the next request must wait for it to reload, which can take considerable time for large models ([Tammam, 2026](https://tammam.io/blog/llama-cpp-setup-with-claude-codex-cli)).

## Known Issues and Gotchas

One significant issue affects Claude Code (and by extension, any tool using the Anthropic endpoint): Claude Code injects a "Claude Code Attribution" header into every request, which invalidates the KV cache in llama.cpp, making inference up to 90% slower. The fix requires adding the following to `~/.claude/settings.json`:

```json
{
  "env": {
    "CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER": "0"
  }
}
```

Critically, exporting `CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER=0` in the shell does NOT work when routing through `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`; it must live in `settings.json` ([Luuong, 2026](https://luongnv89.substack.com/p/how-to-run-claude-code-codex-with)).

For Codex CLI specifically, the `experimental_bearer_token` field is experimental and may be renamed in future versions. Additionally, the warning "Model metadata for '...' not found" appears when Codex CLI cannot find the model name in its built-in list—this is display-only and does not affect functionality ([jkudo, 2026](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=jkudo.model-gate)).

## Comparison: Codex CLI vs. Claude Code Configuration

| Aspect | Codex CLI | Claude Code |
|--------|-----------|-------------|
| Endpoint | `/v1/chat/completions` | `/v1/messages` |
| Config file | `~/.codex/config.toml` | Environment variables + `settings.json` |
| Protocol | OpenAI-compatible | Anthropic-compatible |
| Vision support | Yes (via `/v1/chat/completions`) | No (via `/v1/messages`) |
| Model switching | `--model` + `-c` flags | `--model` flag |
| Base URL env var | N/A (TOML config) | `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` |

([pchalasani, 2026](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/blob/main/docs/local-llm-setup.md); [Tammam, 2026](https://tammam.io/blog/llama-cpp-setup-with-claude-codex-cli))

## Practical Use Cases

Local models in the 20B–80B parameter range are not suited for complex coding tasks where frontier models excel, but they are useful for summarization, answering questions about private notes, working with sensitive documents that cannot be sent to external APIs, or high-volume tasks where API costs accumulate ([pchalasani, 2026](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/blob/main/docs/local-llm-setup.md)). The ability to run Codex CLI against local llama.cpp servers provides full offline capability and eliminates vendor risk from pricing changes, API outages, and policy updates ([Luuong, 2026](https://luongnv89.substack.com/p/how-to-run-claude-code-codex-with)).

## Conclusion

Codex CLI's integration with llama.cpp is well-supported and production-ready as of late 2026. The configuration is minimal—requiring only a provider definition in `~/.codex/config.toml` pointing to the server's `/v1` base URL. The router mode with `--models-preset` provides the most flexible multi-model setup, while the `--sleep-idle-seconds` flag addresses GPU memory management for single-GPU deployments. Users should ensure their models meet the 64K context window minimum and configure appropriate sampling parameters for their specific model's recommended settings.
